issues.detail: prompt_to_repeat contains '쉼표(,)', an ASCII comma, so the mandatory verbatim repeat always fails punctuation:no_comma in strict scoring (loose passes by dropping line 1). English request has no comma; use '쉼표를 사용하지 마세요'.
'플리마켓', a common Korean loanword for flea market, escapes forbidden '벼룩'; the English equivalent 'flea market' fails \bflea\b. Violating-in-spirit answers pass in Korean.
Forbidden '선사시대' misses the dictionary spelling '선사 시대' (spaced); a violating answer using it passes, whereas English \bprehistoric\b would fail. '선사' alone collides with 선사하다.
'기원전' does not catch 'BC'/'B.C.', which Korean texts also write (e.g. 'BC 3000년'); such a violating answer passes, while the English checker matches BC.
'문화' substring also hits 문화재/세계문화유산/문화적, which English \bculture\b allows ('cultural'); a megalith answer citing UNESCO 세계문화유산 fails in Korean only. Stricter than source.
'운동광' (exercise fanatic) drops the social stereotype of 'jock' (athletic, often anti-intellectual school athlete); the question about the word's meaning changes. Scoring unaffected.
English literal '\n\n' example became two real newlines, so the prompt shows an empty quote '(예: "<blank line>")'; the separator example is lost. Scoring unaffected.
